Conformal Inference Frameworks

Methodology and Comparative Analysis for Uncertainty Estimation

Silvia Duque Moro

library(ranger)
library(quantregForest)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# Load the clean dataset
df <- read.csv("../nhanes_final.csv")
set.seed(1)

n_total <- nrow(df)

# Generate random indices to ensure data exchangeability across splits
indices <- sample(seq_len(n_total))

# Define partition split points (60% Train / 20% Calibration / 20% Test)
cut_train <- round(0.60 * n_total)
cut_calib <- round(0.80 * n_total)

# Construct data subsets
train_df <- df[indices[1:cut_train], ]
cal_df   <- df[indices[(cut_train + 1):cut_calib], ]
test_df  <- df[indices[(cut_calib + 1):n_total], ]

Simple Split Conformal

# 1. Model Training on the Training Set
rf_simple <- ranger(LBXSCR ~ ., data = train_df)

# 2. Generate Predictions on the Calibration Set
pred_cal <- predict(rf_simple, data = cal_df)$predictions

# 3. Compute Non-Conformity Scores (Absolute Residuals)
scores_simple <- abs(cal_df$LBXSCR - pred_cal)

# 4. Calculate the Conformal Quantile
alpha <- 0.05 # 95% Target Confidence Level
n_cal <- length(scores_simple)
q_hat_simple <- quantile(scores_simple, probs = ceiling((n_cal + 1) * (1 - alpha)) / n_cal)

# 5. Generate Predictions on the Test Set
pred_test <- predict(rf_simple, data = test_df)$predictions

# 6. Estimate Conditional Variance (Sigma) for Heteroscedasticity Analysis
train_pred <- predict(rf_simple, data = train_df)$predictions
res_train <- abs(train_df$LBXSCR - train_pred)
log_res_train <- log(res_train + 1e-6) # Log-transform absolute residuals to ensure positivity
train_df_sigma <- train_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(log_res = log_res_train)
rf_sigma_log <- ranger(log_res ~ ., data = train_df_sigma)
sigma_test <- predict(rf_sigma_log, data = test_df)$predictions

# 7. Construct Prediction Intervals (Constant Bandwidth / Margins)
test_results_simple <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    pred = pred_test,
    lower = pred - q_hat_simple,
    upper = pred + q_hat_simple,
    covered = LBXSCR >= lower & LBXSCR <= upper,
    sigma_est = sigma_test,
    width = upper - lower
  )

# 8. Compute Conformal Evaluation Metrics
metrics_simple <- list(
  coverage = mean(test_results_simple$covered),
  average_width = mean(test_results_simple$upper - test_results_simple$lower),
  width_sd = sd(test_results_simple$width)
)

Normalized Split Conformal

# 1. Model Training on the Training Set
rf_mu <- ranger(LBXSCR ~ ., data = train_df)

# 2. Train the Conditional Variance Model (sigma)
train_pred <- predict(rf_mu, data = train_df)$predictions
res_train <- abs(train_df$LBXSCR - train_pred)
log_res_train <- log(res_train + 1e-6) # Log-transform absolute residuals to ensure positivity

train_df_sigma <- train_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(log_res = log_res_train)
rf_sigma_log <- ranger(log_res ~ ., data = train_df_sigma)

# 3. Calibration Phase: Compute Normalized Non-Conformity Scores
mu_cal <- predict(rf_mu, data = cal_df)$predictions
sigma_cal <- exp(predict(rf_sigma_log, data = cal_df)$predictions) # Back-transform from log scale
scores_norm <- abs(cal_df$LBXSCR - mu_cal) / sigma_cal

# 4. Calculate the Conformal Quantile
alpha <- 0.05 # 95% Target Confidence Level
n_cal <- length(scores_norm)
q_hat_norm <- quantile(scores_norm, probs = ceiling((n_cal + 1) * (1 - alpha)) / n_cal)

# 5. Generate Predictions and Variance Estimates on the Test Set
mu_test <- predict(rf_mu, data = test_df)$predictions
sigma_test <- exp(predict(rf_sigma_log, data = test_df)$predictions)

# 6. Construct Locally Adaptive Prediction Intervals
test_results_norm <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    pred = mu_test,
    lower = pred - sigma_test * q_hat_norm,
    upper = pred + sigma_test * q_hat_norm,
    covered = LBXSCR >= lower & LBXSCR <= upper,
    sigma_est = sigma_test,
    width = upper - lower
  )
  
# 7. Compute Conformal Evaluation Metrics
metrics_norm <- list(
  coverage = mean(test_results_norm$covered),
  average_width = mean(test_results_norm$upper - test_results_norm$lower), 
  width_sd = sd(test_results_norm$width)
)

Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)

# 1. Train the Quantile Regression Forest (QRF) on the Training Set
qrf_model <- quantregForest(x = train_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                            y = train_df$LBXSCR, 
                            ntree = 500)

# 2. Predict Lower and Upper Quantiles on the Calibration Set
cal_quantiles <- predict(qrf_model, newdata = cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                         what = c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2))

# 3. Compute CQR Non-Conformity Scores
# Measures the signed distance to the predicted quantile boundaries: max(q_low - y, y - q_high)
scores_cqr <- pmax(cal_quantiles[, 1] - cal_df$LBXSCR, 
                   cal_df$LBXSCR - cal_quantiles[, 2])

# 4. Calculate the Conformal Quantile
n_cal <- length(scores_cqr)
q_hat_cqr <- quantile(scores_cqr, probs = ceiling((n_cal + 1) * (1 - alpha)) / n_cal)

# 5. Predict Lower and Upper Quantiles on the Test Set
test_quantiles <- predict(qrf_model, newdata = test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                          what = c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2))

# 6. Construct Conformalized Quantile Regression Intervals
test_results_cqr <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    lower = test_quantiles[, 1] - q_hat_cqr,
    upper = test_quantiles[, 2] + q_hat_cqr,
    pred = (lower + upper) / 2, # Midpoint serves as the point prediction proxy
    covered = LBXSCR >= lower & LBXSCR <= upper,
    width = upper - lower
  )
  
# 7. Compute Conformal Evaluation Metrics
metrics_cqr <- list(
  coverage = mean(test_results_cqr$covered),
  average_width = mean(test_results_cqr$width),
  width_sd = sd(test_results_cqr$width)
)

Weighted Conformal Prediction (WCP)

# 1. Model Training on the Training Set
rf_wcp <- ranger(LBXSCR ~ ., data = train_df)

# 2. Generate Predictions and Compute Absolute Residuals on the Calibration Set
pred_cal_wcp <- predict(rf_wcp, data = cal_df)$predictions
scores_cal_wcp <- abs(cal_df$LBXSCR - pred_cal_wcp)

# 3. Estimate Weights via Propensity Scores (Calibration vs. Test)
df_shift <- rbind(
  cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(is_test = 0),
  test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(is_test = 1)
)
df_shift$is_test <- as.factor(df_shift$is_test)

# Train probabilistic classifier
prob_model <- ranger(is_test ~ ., data = df_shift, probability = TRUE, num.trees = 100)

# Function to compute Likelihood Ratio Weights (Odds)
calcular_pesos_w <- function(data_frame) {
  p_hat <- predict(prob_model, data = data_frame)$predictions[, "1"]
  p_hat <- pmin(pmax(p_hat, 0.001), 0.999) # Clipping to prevent infinity
  return(p_hat / (1 - p_hat))
}

w_cal <- calcular_pesos_w(cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR))
w_test_vec <- calcular_pesos_w(test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR))

# 4. Calculate Weighted Quantiles per Test Instance
alpha <- 0.05
n_test <- nrow(test_df)

# Sort calibration elements based on non-conformity scores
ord_cal  <- order(scores_cal_wcp)
s_sorted <- scores_cal_wcp[ord_cal]
w_sorted <- w_cal[ord_cal]

# Create matrices for parallel computation
W_cal_mat  <- matrix(w_sorted, nrow = length(w_sorted), ncol = n_test)
W_test_mat <- matrix(w_test_vec, nrow = length(w_sorted), ncol = n_test, byrow = TRUE)

# Calculate probability denominators and cumulative distribution functions
sum_w_vector <- sum(w_sorted) + w_test_vec
P_mat     <- t(t(W_cal_mat) / sum_w_vector)
P_cum_mat <- apply(P_mat, 2, cumsum)

# Identify indices where the cumulative probability exceeds the critical threshold
idx_q_vec <- apply(P_cum_mat, 2, function(col) which(col >= (1 - alpha))[1])
idx_q_vec[is.na(idx_q_vec)] <- length(s_sorted) # Boundary fallback

# Extract localized quantiles for each test point
q_hat_wcp_vec <- s_sorted[idx_q_vec]

# 5. Generate Point Predictions on the Test Set
pred_test_wcp <- predict(rf_wcp, data = test_df)$predictions

# 6. Construct Weighted Prediction Intervals
test_results_wcp <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    pred = pred_test_wcp,
    lower = pred - q_hat_wcp_vec,
    upper = pred + q_hat_wcp_vec,
    covered = LBXSCR >= lower & LBXSCR <= upper,
    width = upper - lower
  )

# 7. Compute Conformal Evaluation Metrics
metrics_wcp <- list(
  coverage = mean(test_results_wcp$covered),
  average_width = mean(test_results_wcp$width),
  width_sd = sd(test_results_wcp$width)
)

Weighted Conformalized Quantile Regression (Weighted CQR)

# 1. Train the Base Distributional Model (Quantile Regression Forest)
qrf_model <- quantregForest(x = train_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                            y = train_df$LBXSCR, 
                            ntree = 500)

# 2. Compute CQR Non-Conformity Scores on the Calibration Set
cal_quantiles <- predict(qrf_model, newdata = cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                         what = c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2))
cal_quantiles <- as.matrix(cal_quantiles)
scores_cqr_wcp <- pmax(cal_quantiles[, 1] - cal_df$LBXSCR, 
                       cal_df$LBXSCR - cal_quantiles[, 2])

# 3. Estimate Weights via Propensity Scores (Calibration vs. Test)
df_shift <- rbind(
  cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(is_test = 0),
  test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR) %>% mutate(is_test = 1)
)
df_shift$is_test <- as.factor(df_shift$is_test)

prob_model <- ranger(is_test ~ ., data = df_shift, probability = TRUE, num.trees = 100)

calcular_pesos_w <- function(data_frame) {
  p_hat <- predict(prob_model, data = data_frame)$predictions[, "1"]
  p_hat <- pmin(pmax(p_hat, 0.001), 0.999) # Clipping to prevent infinity
  return(p_hat / (1 - p_hat))
}

w_cal <- calcular_pesos_w(cal_df %>% select(-LBXSCR))
w_test_vec <- calcular_pesos_w(test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR))

# 4. Calculate Weighted Quantiles per Test Instance 
ord_cal   <- order(scores_cqr_wcp)
s_sorted  <- scores_cqr_wcp[ord_cal]
w_sorted  <- w_cal[ord_cal]

W_cal_mat  <- matrix(w_sorted, nrow = length(w_sorted), ncol = n_test)
sum_w_vector <- sum(w_sorted) + w_test_vec

P_mat     <- t(t(W_cal_mat) / sum_w_vector)
P_cum_mat <- apply(P_mat, 2, cumsum)

idx_q_vec <- apply(P_cum_mat, 2, function(col) which(col >= (1 - alpha))[1])
idx_q_vec[is.na(idx_q_vec)] <- length(s_sorted) # Boundary fallback

q_hat_weighted_cqr <- s_sorted[idx_q_vec]

# 5. Predict Base Quantiles on the Test Set
test_quantiles <- predict(qrf_model, newdata = test_df %>% select(-LBXSCR), 
                          what = c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2))
test_quantiles <- as.matrix(test_quantiles)

# 6. Construct Adaptive and Weighted Hybrid Prediction Intervals
test_results_weighted_cqr <- test_df %>%
  mutate(
    lower = test_quantiles[, 1] - q_hat_weighted_cqr,
    upper = test_quantiles[, 2] + q_hat_weighted_cqr,
    pred = (lower + upper) / 2, 
    covered = LBXSCR >= lower & LBXSCR <= upper,
    width = upper - lower
  )

# 7. Compute Conformal Evaluation Metrics
metrics_weighted_cqr <- list(
  coverage = mean(test_results_weighted_cqr$covered),
  average_width = mean(test_results_weighted_cqr$width),
  width_sd = sd(test_results_weighted_cqr$width)
)

Coverage and Efficiency Comparison

# 1. Consolidate raw validation metrics
tabla_sencilla <- tibble(
  Method = c(
    "Simple Split Conformal",
    "Normalized Split Conformal",
    "Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)",
    "Weighted Conformal Prediction (WCP)",
    "Weighted CQR (Hybrid)"
  ),
  Coverage = c(
    metrics_simple$coverage,
    metrics_norm$coverage,
    metrics_cqr$coverage,
    metrics_wcp$coverage,
    metrics_weighted_cqr$coverage
  ),
  Avg_Width = c(
    metrics_simple$average_width,
    metrics_norm$average_width,
    metrics_cqr$average_width,
    metrics_wcp$average_width,
    metrics_weighted_cqr$average_width
  ),
  Width_SD = c(
    metrics_simple$width_sd,
    metrics_norm$width_sd,
    metrics_cqr$width_sd,
    metrics_wcp$width_sd,
    metrics_weighted_cqr$width_sd
  )
)

# 2. Format metrics and render HTML table
tabla_sencilla %>%
  mutate(
    `Empirical Coverage` = scales::percent(Coverage, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Average Width (SD)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", Avg_Width, Width_SD)
  ) %>%
  select(Method, `Empirical Coverage`, `Average Width (SD)`) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "c", "c")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  )

Adaptability and Conditional Coverage Analysis

Simple Split Conformal

# Approximate conditional coverage

# Create uncertainty deciles
plot_data <- test_results_simple %>%
  mutate(
    uncertainty_bin = cut(sigma_est, 
                          breaks = quantile(sigma_est, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.1)), 
                          include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(uncertainty_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    actual_coverage = mean(covered),
    n = n()
  )

# Lollipop plot of the empirical coverage rate
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = factor(uncertainty_bin), y = actual_coverage)) +
  # Dashed line representing the target 95% coverage
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", color = "#444444", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Segments showing the deviation from the 95% target
  geom_segment(aes(xend = factor(uncertainty_bin), 
                   y = 0.95, yend = actual_coverage), color = "#999999", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Points representing the actual coverage per decile
  geom_point(color = "#31688E", size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0.5, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Simple Split Conformal: Conditional Coverage Evaluation",
    x = "Estimated Uncertainty Deciles",
    y = "Empirical Coverage Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "#222222", fill = NA),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold") 
  )

# Interval Width Distribution
# Mean interval width for the reference line
mean_width_simple <- mean(test_results_simple$width)

# Histogram 
ggplot(test_results_simple, aes(x = width)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#31688E", color = "#FFFFFF", alpha = 0.85, 
                 bins = 30, closed = "left") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_width_simple, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "#444444", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = mean_width_simple + (max(test_results_simple$width) * 0.02), 
           y = Inf, label = paste0("Mean: ", round(mean_width_simple, 3), " mg/dL"), 
           hjust = 0, vjust = 2, color = "#444444", fontface = "italic", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Simple Split Conformal: Interval Width Distribution",
    x = "Interval Width (mg/dL)",
    y = "Absolute Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "#222222", fill = NA)
  )

  labs(
    title = "Locally Adaptive Split Conformal: Interval Width Distribution",
    x = "Interval Width (mg/dL)",
    y = "Absolute Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "#222222", fill = NA)
  )

Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)

# Approximate conditional coverage

plot_data_cqr <- test_results_cqr %>%
  mutate(
    # CQR uncertainty is represented by the difference between estimated quantiles
    uncertainty_cqr = test_quantiles[, 2] - test_quantiles[, 1],
    uncertainty_bin = cut(uncertainty_cqr, 
                          breaks = quantile(uncertainty_cqr, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.1)), 
                          include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(uncertainty_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    actual_coverage = mean(covered),
    n = n()
  )

ggplot(plot_data_cqr, aes(x = factor(uncertainty_bin), y = actual_coverage)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", color = "#444444", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = factor(uncertainty_bin), 
                   y = 0.95, yend = actual_coverage), color = "#999999", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(color = "#31688E", size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0.5, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Conformalized Quantile Regression: Conditional Coverage Evaluation",
    x = "Estimated Uncertainty Deciles",
    y = "Empirical Coverage Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "#222222", fill = NA),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold") 
  )

# Interval Width Distribution

mean_width_cqr <- mean(test_results_cqr$width)

ggplot(test_results_cqr, aes(x = width)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#31688E", color = "#FFFFFF", alpha = 0.85, 
                 bins = 30, closed = "left") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_width_cqr, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "#444444", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = mean_width_cqr + (max(test_results_cqr$width) * 0.02), 
           y = Inf, label = paste0("Mean: ", round(mean_width_cqr, 3), " mg/dL"), 
           hjust = 0, vjust = 2, color = "#444444", fontface = "italic", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Conformalized Quantile Regression: Interval Width Distribution",
    x = "Interval Width (mg/dL)",
    y = "Absolute Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "#222222", fill = NA)
  )
